what_was_done: The two residual holes in the arithmetic/${} judgement are closed. (1) _arithmetic_harmless now also requires the span's inner parentheses to balance: the new _parentheses_balance checks a running depth that never goes below zero and ends at zero, so '$((echo PWNED)|(cat))', the same span in double quotes, '$((a)&&(b))' and '$((id)|(id))' - which sh and bash end at the ')' that closes their second '(' and reparse as command substitutions - count as substitutions and are opaque, while '$(( (1+2)*3 ))' and '$(((1+2)))' stay plain arithmetic. (2) The '${...}' span now counts as a substitution unless its inner text is plain, decided by the new _parameter_plain (replacing _holds_substitution): letters, digits, '_ - . , / : = + % # @ ? ! ~', blanks, $name and plain arithmetic spans only - any quote, backslash, backslash escape, nested '${' or parenthesis makes it a substitution, so "${y:-'}'$(id)}" (the quoted brace ends the span early for the parser while the shell reads past it) and zsh's '${(e):-\$\(id\)}' are opaque, and '${y:-$((1+2))}' stays judgeable. Verified through the runner: an agent's 'vsdd survey $((id)|(id))' and the other new forms produce no marker, no permissionDecision and no updatedInput (asserted in test_caller.py::test_decision_pairing). New opaque cases in test_shell.py::test_substitution_beside_arithmetic_in_one_word_is_opaque: the six forms above, with '$(( (1+2)*3 ))' added to the judgeable list. Mutation checks (in a scratch copy): dropping _parentheses_balance from _arithmetic_harmless fails the shell test and test_decision_pairing; short-circuiting _parameter_plain fails the shell test.

The bracket-expression branch of _read_word is gone: a '[' now only marks the word expanded and the loop reads what follows as anywhere else, so blanks, joiners, '$(' and backticks after it split words and show substitutions exactly as shells read them. A '$[' counts as a substitution (the word loop cannot follow bash and zsh arithmetic's extent), which pins the form $['$(id)'] - bash and zsh run the substitution inside the quoted span (verified: 'echo $[77 + $(id)]' in bash prints id's output), and without the flag the single-quote branch would swallow it unseen. New test test_shell.py::test_brackets_split_or_are_opaque: '[ ; id ; ]', '[;id;]', '[ && id ]', 'a[b|id]', '[$(id)]', '[`id`]', '$[$(id)]' and '$[\'$(id)\']' each split into segments or are opaque, while 'a[bc]' stays a judgeable one-segment glob. Agent cases added to test_caller.py::test_decision_pairing: '[;id;]', '[$(id)]' and '$[$(id)]' get no marker, no decision, no rewrite. Mutation checks (scratch copy): restoring the swallow-to-']' branch fails the test; dropping the '$[' flag fails it (through the $['$(id)'] case).

'\r' is removed from the lexer's blank set and from _WORD_END, so a carriage return is the ordinary word character sh, bash, dash and zsh read: 'vsdd survey \r#; id' now parses as two segments ('\r#' is a word, so '#' starts no comment and the second command is seen) and is_vsdd_call is False - an agent cannot hide a command behind a carriage return any more. New test test_shell.py::test_carriage_return_is_a_word_character asserts the two-segment parse with programs ['vsdd', 'id'] and that 'echo a\rb' is one word ('a\rb'). An agent case ('vsdd survey \r#; id') was added to test_caller.py::test_decision_pairing: no marker, no decision. Mutation check (scratch copy): restoring '\r' to the blank set and _WORD_END fails the test (the parse collapses to one segment again).

_redirect_op now lets any run of digits hugging a redirect operator be its fd, as POSIX io_number allows: the 'probe - index == 1' restriction is gone, the op carries the whole digit run ('10>'), and the lexer's digit-lookahead condition (the new _fd_hugs_redirect) scans the whole run before checking for '<>' - previously '10>/dev/null cmd arg' entered no redirect branch at all because only one digit was peeked. '10>/dev/null cmd arg' parses as program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirect ('10>', '/dev/null'), so a future Bash rule judges the real program; under dash and zsh the command only fails to find a program named with digits, the safe reading. Added to test_shell.py::test_leading_redirect_before_the_program. Mutation checks (scratch copy): restoring 'probe - index == 1' in _redirect_op, and restoring the single-char peek in the lexer condition, each fail the test.
